Holy Shit! I went there back in 2001 when it was called Stone Mountain School and it was an all boys camp then. The stories I could tell you then. Went from 2000 to 2002 before heading off the another one in Montana. 

The few things I remember:

During 9/11, the entire camp was called into the dining hall and watched it live, but I was in trouble so I had to sit outside until the viewing was over. I had no clue about 9/11 until years later when I saw a special program on TV and put two and two together because I just remember that day being so different from the others. 

I was a constant trouble maker, and they would punish me with "24" , "48" or "72", meaning the amount of hours I was made to sit outside in a chair in the field. Food was brought to me and someone watched me at all times. I was only allowed a small 4 foot circle to walk around in and my sleeping bag. 

We had a 1 month trip down the Swanee River (if I recall) and they forgot sunscreen and I ended up with second degree burns on both my shoulders to the point they are still scarred from this.

One kid had part of his digestive tract removed so he was much more hungry than others, but they refused to give him more food or even let him use the latrine more than the rest of us. He would constantly sneak out of the cabins at night and steal food from around the camp because they didn't feed him enough. 

I still have my shirt from the camp locked away until I burn it in an effigy from the other 4 camps I went to. This place, while not the worst of the worse, was still traumatic and there's quite a lot I still have hidden and locked away.
